<document id="disputes-provisional-credit">
Provisional credit during a dispute
A provisional credit is money we put back in your account while we investigate a dispute. It lets you use the money without waiting for the final outcome.

## When you get it

If your dispute passes an initial review, the provisional credit arrives within 10 business days of filing. It shows in your activity as "Provisional credit" with the merchant name.

## How long the investigation takes

Most disputes are resolved within 45 days. For foreign transactions, and for accounts open less than 30 days, it can take up to 90 days.

## If the dispute goes your way

The provisional credit becomes permanent. You don't need to do anything.

## If it doesn't

We send you a written explanation and take the provisional credit back 5 business days after that notice. If that makes your balance negative, you'll need to add money.

Not every dispute gets a provisional credit. For example, we may wait for the merchant's response if you already received a refund for part of the purchase.

Still stuck? Chat with us in the app. Someone is there around the clock.
</document>
<document id="disputes-how-to-file">
How to file a dispute
Most disputes can be filed yourself in the app in a couple of minutes. Support can also file one for you.

## File it yourself

1. Tap the transaction in your activity feed.
2. Tap Get help and choose the reason.
3. Answer the questions and add any documents.

## Before you file

- The transaction must have posted. Pending transactions can't be disputed.
- Unauthorized transactions: within 60 days of the statement date, and the card must be frozen or reported first.
- Merchant problems: within 120 days of the transaction date, after contacting the merchant.

## Filing through support

Support can open disputes totaling up to $5,000 per case. Larger cases go to our Disputes team, who will contact you within 2 business days.

## One dispute per transaction

If a transaction already has an open dispute, add information to that case instead of opening a new one.

Still stuck? Chat with us in the app. Someone is there around the clock.
</document>
<document id="cushion-negative-after-dispute">
Negative balance after a dispute
Your balance can go negative when we take back a provisional credit after a dispute is denied, or when a deposit is returned. This isn't Cushion, and it can happen on any plan, including Basic.

## Why it happens

A provisional credit is money we lend you while a dispute is investigated. If the dispute is denied, we give you written notice and take it back 5 business days later. If you've spent it in the meantime, the balance can drop below zero.

## What to do

Add money to bring your balance back to zero. Any incoming deposit repays it automatically.

## Fees

There are no fees for a negative balance ($0.00).

## If it isn't repaid

As with Cushion, if a negative balance lasts 60 days, the account is restricted until it's repaid. On Plus and Premium, Cushion is suspended while the balance is negative for longer than 30 days.

## Can't pay it right away?

Message support. If you're going through financial hardship, we can pass your case to our Account Services team.

Still stuck? Chat with us in the app. Someone is there around the clock.
</document>
</documents>

Customer question: when will i get my money back after filing a dispute
